messages:
Jordan (oncall): ⚠️ Seeing a sudden increase in 5xx for hosted /v1/generate (eu-west) starting ~09:12 UTC. Error mix: 502 gateway + some 504s. P50 latency fine, p95 spikes. Impacting a handful of paying customers.
Maya (sre): on it, grabbing traces. Any recent deploys or routing changes?
Jordan (oncall): Noted a config push to gateway routing at 09:05 UTC for model alias 'redwood-tiny-v2' -> canary. Could be coincident.
Liam (eng-runtime): I see amplified backend timeouts from the runtime pool handling long-context requests. KV cache miss rate jumped ~3x. Attaching quick logs:
```
[09:13:21] request_id=tx-9a1f timeout waiting for backend response (shard-12)
[09:13:22] backend=runtime-22 connection reset by peer
[09:13:23] retrying request (attempt 2)
```

Nina (engineer): re: canary, the alias change included a new batching policy tweak. If batching is mis-tuned for short requests it can cause backend stalls.
Rachel (support): Customer thread: ACME Inc reports 502 on all POST /v1/generate calls since ~09:14. They're escalating to CSM. Preparing a calm comms update.
Maya (sre): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable the routing change (roll back alias) 2) increase gateway per-request timeout to allow slow backends to finish for short period 3) enable fallback to a stable small model for high-error rate customers. Which we can flip from console.
Liam (eng-runtime): I can flip the alias back now. Will also roll a conservative batching parameter to previous value.
Jordan (oncall): Go ahead Liam. Nina can you prepare a one-liner revert playbook so support can explain?
Nina (engineer): On it. Revert steps (will paste to #runbooks after):
```
1. Console -> Model routing -> alias redwood-tiny-v2 -> revert to stable-20240512
2. Gateway -> config -> timeout-ms = 12000 -> set back to 10000 (temporary raise)
3. If errors persist, flip per-customer fallback to redwood-mini (console -> fallbacks)
```

Liam (eng-runtime): Revert pushed for alias, change active in eu-west in ~30s. Rolling batching policy back as well.
incident-bot: rollback of routing alias redwood-tiny-v2 confirmed by deploy-bot (deploy-98765) at 09:18:03 UTC :white_check_mark:
Jordan (oncall): Monitoring error rate...
[09:19] error rate down ~60% for affected customers. Some residual 504s from inflight backpressure.
Rachel (support): Sent update to ACME: we're rolling back a recent routing change and monitoring; ETA 15-30m. They acknowledged.
Maya (sre): Next steps: collect sample traces for 09:05-09:20 window, KV cache metrics, and batching latency histograms. Also check host OOMs / connection resets.
Nina (engineer): I dumped a runtime shard threadstack and saw a KV cache eviction storm concurrent with canary traffic. Likely batching size spike caused more concurrency and spilled memory, causing GC pauses.
Liam (eng-runtime): Confirmed a single host had elevated GC (heap pressure) and started dropping connections ~09:12. We'll cordon host and drain.
Jordan (oncall): Good. I'm switching incident to short war room for follow-up actions and postmortem. Assigning action items now.
Rachel (support): I'll open a support ticket update and add the CSM notes, include root cause summary once we have traces.
Maya (sre): For postmortem: timeline + root cause hypothesis (batching param + KV cache eviction -> GC -> connection resets -> gateway 502/504), list of mitigations executed, and permanent remediation.
Nina (engineer): Proposed permanent fixes: 1) add safety cap to batching policy based on request-context distribution 2) kv cache soft-eviction under burst 3) better per-host memory alerts 4) include canary perf gate that checks KV miss and heap before alias change.
Liam (eng-runtime): I'll PR batching cap and a canary health check to block routing flips. Nina and I will pair on KV behavior changes.
Jordan (oncall): Quick customer note drafted for Rachel: "We've identified a recent routing change to a canary model that increased backend batching, triggering memory pressure on a small number of runtime hosts; we rolled back the change and errors are reduced. We'll follow up with a timeline and fix plan." Approve?
Rachel (support): Approve. I'll send now.
incident-bot: incident severity lowered to S2 at 09:28 UTC after error rate reduced and fallbacks in place.
Jordan (oncall): Action items summarised:
- Liam: PR batching-safety + canary perf gate (owner) — due EOD tomorrow
- Nina: KV cache soft-eviction design doc + alerts (owner) — due in 3 days
- Maya: Postmortem writeup draft (owner) — due in 48h
- Rachel: Customer communications & ticket closure (owner) — keep CSM loop, update in 1h
- Oncall rotation: add runbook step to check householding of canary changes (owner: Jordan) — due next week

Maya (sre): Recording logs and traces to incident recording. We'll reconvene in ~24h for postmortem review.
Jordan (oncall): Thanks team, nice quick rollback and customer comms. Closing war room thread for now. :white_check_mark:
Rachel (support): Leaving a short customer-facing summary in the ticket and closing after CSM ack.
Nina (engineer): I'll attach the KV trace dump to the postmortem.
Liam (eng-runtime): Follow-ups created in GH and pinned to the incident.
Jordan (oncall): last note: if anyone sees residual 502s after 10:00, ping me directly.
Rachel (support): ack.
